summary: Production 5xx spike: SSL renegotiation flood causes accept-queue growth and upstream runtime soft-resets for QuantaDocs
description: Issue summary: At ~2026-03-10 11:25 UTC we observed a sudden increase in 5xx errors for QuantaDocs traffic routed through the api-gateway in us-west-2. Impact: customers experienced elevated 502/503 rates for chat and embedding endpoints (~12% error rate for a 5-minute window), degraded p99 latency, and several serving runtimes observed GPU soft-resets. Environment: prod-us-west (dedicated pool for QuantaDocs, reserved capacity), api-gateway fronting tenant-specific routes. Observed behaviour: api-gateway accept-queue depth increased, many connections entered a TLS renegotiation loop (re-handshakes), gateway returned 502/503 to clients while upstream runtimes logged watchdog restarts and GPU soft-reset messages. Expected behaviour: TLS sessions should reuse tickets and not cause accept queue growth; runtimes should not receive clustered bursts of new TLS handshakes leading to resource exhaustion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route sustained simulated client traffic (long-polling + frequent short streams) to customer's dedicated route in us-west-2
2) Force client to rotate TLS session tickets every ~5s to emulate problematic client behavior
3) Observe accept-queue growth on api-gateway and rising 502/503 rates within 2-3 minutes
4) Monitor serving-runtime logs for repeated nvml/gpu soft-reset and watchdog ejection messages
logs: [2026-03-10T11:27:05Z] runtime-worker-17 gpu0: NVML: GPU soft reset triggered (driver_recoverable=1)
[2026-03-10T11:27:08Z] runtime-main watchdog: ejected worker due to repeated handshake stalls (reason=handshake-timeout)
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: correlation between 5xx spike and elevated TLS renegotiation metrics on the gateway (tls_reneg_count spiked ~x40 vs baseline)
SRE confirmed accept-queue growth preceded runtime errors; backlog caused slow socket handoff to upstreams, amplifying retries
Runtime team noticed repeated kernel selection for quantized path on open/llama2-13b-quant that increased CPU-to-GPU scheduling latency under high connection churn
Network team found NAT port exhaustion on the dedicated VPC egress path when clients aggressively rotated TLS tickets, exacerbating accept queue backlog

Hypothesis: a combination of client-side TLS ticket churn + gateway keepalive settings caused repeated new TLS handshakes. This amplified proxy CPU usage and delayed handoffs, leading to runtime worker starvation and eventual GPU soft-resets during heavy model kernel swaps.
mitigation: 1) Immediately enabled a temporary rate-limit on per-connection TLS renegotiations at api-gateway (hotfix applied to ingress policy)
2) Rerouted QuantaDocs traffic to a warmed fallback variant: redwood/ultra-chat-v1:quant-lite in us-west-2 while we stabilized the primary pool
3) Increased apigw accept-queue size and tuned keepalive_timeouts to encourage session reuse for the customer route
4) Applied ephemeral scaling to dedicated pool ( +2 ephemeral GPUs) to absorb immediate load while averting autoscaler oscillation
5) Opened a private support note with QuantaDocs recommending client TLS session reuse and distributing SDK patch to reduce ticket rotation frequency
next_steps: A) Implement longer TLS ticket grace in api-gateway (engineering RFC in progress)
B) Add end-to-end test in CI that simulates TLS-ticket churn combined with mixed streaming/batch workload to catch regressions
C) Runtime: investigate kernel selection path under connection churn and add a guard to avoid expensive kernel swaps during handshake storms
D) Networking: review NAT port allocation for dedicated VPCs and propose mitigation (source port pooling / ephemeral SNAT increase)
E) Follow up with QuantaDocs to validate SDK update and monitor for recurrence for 48h

postmortem_action_items: 1) Runbook update: add section for TLS renegotiation storms and recommended api-gateway mitigations
2) Engineering: land PR to add TLS ticket-grace config and CI test (PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/apigw/pull/4123)
3) Runtime: add monitoring for kernel-swap latency under high connection churn and implement fallback throttling
4) Customer success: schedule a debrief with QuantaDocs and confirm permanent SDK update deployment
